paper_metadata.title: Occupational class differences in outcomes after ischemic stroke: a prospective observational study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large multicenter prospective cohort (IIPAIS) with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and well-defined recruitment across multiple regions in China. Baseline characteristics are thoroughly described.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: It recruited a total of 1711 patients aged ≥40 years with first-ever ischemic stroke from June 2011 to December 2013 in 25 hospitals of five provinces (Jilin, Liaoning, Jiangsu, Hebei and Henan) and two autonomous regions (Inner Mongolia and Ningxia) across China.
items.reasoning: The authors specify age, disease status, time frame, and geographic distribution of the source population.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: All included ischemic stroke patients were confirmed by computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging of the brain within 72 h of symptom onset.
items.reasoning: Recruitment was hospital-based across 25 centers with objective diagnostic confirmation.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: from June 2011 to December 2013
items.reasoning: Specific dates are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria

items.evidence_snippet: IIPAIS excluded patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage, transient ischemic attack, cerebral hemorrhage, or hemorrhage caused by tumor or hematologic diseases, along with pregnant women.
items.reasoning: Clear clinical exclusion criteria are provided to ensure a homogenous ischemic stroke sample.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (occupation) is self-reported and based on 'longest-held' status, which is prone to recall bias. However, the classification system used is standardized.

items.evidence_snippet: we classified occupation into three groups: white-collar workers including office workers, managers and professional technician; blue-collar workers including technicians and machine operators; and farmers.
items.reasoning: The categories are clearly defined based on the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China.

items.reasoning: Self-reporting is a standard but subjective method; 'longest-held' helps reliability but is still subject to recall bias.
